## `mainframe.partition.cpu.capped.count`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.partition.cpu.capped.count` | UpDownCounter | `{cpu}` | The absolute capping limit of the logical partition (LPAR) for the specified processor type, in processors; 0 when absolute capping is not enabled. [1] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[1]:** Classic mode: the logical-partition object properties `absolute-processing-capping` (`cp`), `absolute-ifl-capping` (`ifl`), `absolute-cf-capping` (`icf`), `absolute-ziip-capping` (`iip`) and `absolute-aap-capping` (`aap`). Each is an object with `type` and `value`; `value` is reported when `type` is `processors`, otherwise 0. DPM mode: the partition object properties `cp-absolute-processor-capping-value` (`cp`) and `ifl-absolute-processor-capping-value` (`ifl`), reported when `cp-absolute-processor-capping` or `ifl-absolute-processor-capping` is true, otherwise 0. Caps can be fractional: a cap of half a processor is reported as 0.5. A configured cap is always greater than 0, so 0 means no absolute capping.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`mainframe.cpu.type`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-cpu-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The type of mainframe processor within the Central Processing Complex (CPC). | `all`; `cp`; `icf` |

---

`mainframe.cpu.type` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aap` | Application Assist Processor (AAP), a processor dedicated to accelerating Java and XML processing for database workloads. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `all` | All types of mainframe processors combined. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `cbp` | Container Based Processor (CBP), a processor type for container-based workloads. Present only in HMC/SE versions 2.14.0 through 2.15.0. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `cp` | Central Processor (CP), the general-purpose processor that hosts a mainframe operating system such as z/OS. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `icf` | Integrated Coupling Facility (ICF), a processor dedicated to running coupling facility workloads for high-speed communication between systems in a sysplex. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `ifl` | Integrated Facility for Linux (IFL), a processor dedicated to running Linux workloads on the mainframe. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `iip` | z Integrated Information Processor (zIIP), a processor dedicated to offloading eligible workloads such as Java applications from general-purpose processors. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `sap` | System Assist Processor (SAP), a processor dedicated to system management and I/O processing workloads. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `mainframe.partition.cpu.mode`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.partition.cpu.mode` | Gauge | `1` | The processor allocation mode of the DPM partition as a numeric code (0=shared, 1=dedicated). [2] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[2]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API `partition` object property `processor-mode` (DPM mode only). In shared mode, processor cycles are shared across partitions; in dedicated mode, processors are exclusively assigned to the partition.



## `mainframe.partition.cpu.reserved.count`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.partition.cpu.reserved.count` | UpDownCounter | `{cpu}` | The number of processors of the specified type reserved for the logical partition (LPAR). [3] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[3]:** Reserved processors are allocated to the partition but not yet in active use and are available for dynamic activation. Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API partition object properties `processor-count-<type>-reserved` (all modes). In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to pre-allocated but idle vCPUs.

## `mainframe.partition.cpu.threads_per_processor`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.partition.cpu.threads_per_processor` | Gauge | `{thread}` | The number of simultaneous multithreading (SMT) hardware threads per processor configured for the DPM partition. [4] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[4]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API `partition` object property `threads-per-processor` (DPM mode only). Typical values are 1 (SMT disabled) or 2 (SMT enabled with two hardware threads per physical processor).



## `mainframe.partition.cpu.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.partition.cpu.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time processors of the specified type allocated to the logical partition (LPAR) were busy, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [5] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[5]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API logical-partition-usage metric group (classic mode) fields `cp-processor-usage`, `ifl-processor-usage`, `icf-processor-usage` and `iip-processor-usage` — select with the `mainframe.cpu.type` attribute. In DPM mode the partition-usage metric group (HMC >= 2.13.1) reports only an aggregate `processor-usage` field with no per-type breakdown, so `mainframe.cpu.type` is not set there. The HMC reports an integer percentage (0-100), which is divided by 100 to yield the 0-1 ratio this metric declares. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the per-type CPU utilization of a virtual machine.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`mainframe.cpu.type`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-cpu-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Conditionally Required` [1] | string | The type of mainframe processor within the Central Processing Complex (CPC). | `all`; `cp`; `icf` |

**[1] `mainframe.cpu.type`:** Required in classic mode, where logical-partition-usage reports one field per processor type. Not set in DPM mode, where partition-usage reports a single aggregate processor-usage field.
